summary: Iter171 verified end-to-end. Backend: all 9 iter171 pytest tests green (access-expiring sweep flip + warn+dedupe, digest preview 200/401, JA consent-split comparison/release/status/revoke/403). Regression iter168+169+170 = 35/35 green. Combined 44/44 in ~63s. Direct curl of /api/parent/notification-mode/preview-digest with parent1 JWT returns 200 {delivered:true, source:'demo_sample', event_count:5}; unauth returns 401. Frontend: /for-portal-engineers is public and renders with data-testid=for-portal-engineers-page; all six required sections (portal-eng-title, section-auth, section-permission-check, section-events, section-cli, portal-eng-contact-email) visible; 38 code blocks present (>=5 required); no horizontal overflow at 1920px nor 390px (scrollWidth==clientWidth==390). /shared-with-professionals renders 'Send me a test digest' button (data-testid=notification-mode-preview) inside notification-mode-card; JS-triggered click fires POST /api/parent/notification-mode/preview-digest -> 200 with expected payload — integration verified.

issues: Global 'Just so we're on the same page' disclaimer modal overlays the page and intercepts real user clicks (a native Playwright .click(force=True) landed on a Privacy Policy link inside the modal instead of the underlying button). This is a pre-existing app-wide modal — not new in iter171 — but it does block first-interaction clicks on the new 'Send me a test digest' button until the user acknowledges. Consider suppressing this modal on the public /for-portal-engineers route (external portal engineers shouldn't see a legal-disclaimer overlay before they can read the contract docs).

action_items: Optional: suppress the global legal-disclaimer modal on the public /for-portal-engineers route so external portal engineers can read the handshake docs without dismissing it.

Optional: on /shared-with-professionals, the disclaimer modal should be dismissed before rendering interactive controls, OR the notification-mode card should be pushed below the fold — currently a first-time user's click on 'Send me a test digest' is captured by the modal.
critical_code_review_comments: access_expiring_sweep.flip_expired_invitations correctly cascades to professional_report_permissions and is idempotent — verified.
_iter_warning_candidates uses a ±24h band and dedupes via access_expiring_warning_sends collection — dedupe path verified by dry-run twice.
parent_professional_invitations.preview-digest handler returns source='demo_sample' + event_count=5 for a user with zero recent events — matches spec.

joint_alignment_routes consent-split: comparison_eligible is only True when BOTH parents consented AND neither revoked; release_eligible additionally requires SAME professional_name — behaviour matched by the 9-test suite.
Revoke branch preserves historical consented_at and only writes revoked_at (audit-trail spec) — verified by test_revoke_comparison_clears_eligibility_flag.
seed_data_creation: Pytest fixtures create TEST_ prefixed users + JA cases per test; nothing manual.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter171 is fully working. All four backlog items delivered: (1) preview-digest endpoint 200/401 with demo_sample fallback, (2) public /for-portal-engineers page overflow-free at 390px + 1920px with 38 copyable code blocks, (3) access-expiring sweep flip + warn+dedupe pure-Python functions all pass (background loop stays idle unless ACCESS_EXPIRING_SWEEP_ENABLED=1), (4) JA consent-split (comparison + release + status + revoke) with per-parent scoping and rollup eligibility flags. Only cosmetic caveat is the global disclaimer modal intercepting first-click on any page — pre-existing, not iter171.
